prompt: A desktop web landing page for Madeform, an independent web design studio in Hyderabad, India, rendered edge to edge at 16:9 desktop proportions with crisp readable typography and no browser frame, monitor, or desk around it. Madeform designs custom websites (from ₹7,999) and mobile QR digital menus (₹2,999 for up to 30 items, ₹50 per extra item) for cafés, bakeries, and local businesses, backed by its live Aster Coffee studio concept. The page is offer-and-proof led, constructed like a specialty coffee roastery pouch whose front carries a large die-cut tasting spec label that functions as the interactive studio front. Along the top bar sits the Madeform mark and wordmark in off-white, 'Hyderabad, India', navigation links Work, Services & pricing, Studio, and a marigold-sealed Let’s talk button. Spanning the main viewport over a deep matte forest-slate ground sits a commanding notched unbleached-paper spec label divided by crisp hairline batch rules: its upper band sets the headline 'A little more you, online.' in bold geometric display type alongside a crisp studio introduction; its middle tasting-grid band pairs two transparent lot specs side by side—Lot 01 Digital Menus ₹2,999 (30 items · table QR) and Lot 02 Business Websites from ₹7,999 (full custom site)—with a cobalt-inked primary button 'Start a project ↗' and 'See full comparison'; tucked cleanly into the label's lower-right window is a sunlit editorial frame of the Aster Coffee website and vermilion menu card marked 'Studio concept'. Below the die-cut bottom edge, the dark forest ground continues into the opening heading of the Aster Coffee case study section. Concrete visual law: deep botanical forest-slate (#1b3b2b) owns the full-bleed background while unbleached cotton label stock (#f3efe6) carries the primary working surface; near-black espresso ink (#161a17) sets clean sturdy neo-grotesque headlines and tabular figures, batch-stamp cobalt (#1c4fd7) anchors interactive controls and lot codes, and harvest marigold (#e8a317) seals the primary status accents. Signature element: notched die-cut label corners and ruled batch-lot metadata bands.
